message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno deck).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s an action card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a direction‑changing card is played). On your turn you may:
1. **Play** one card that matches the color, number, or symbol of the top discard.
2. **Draw** one card from the draw pile if you cannot play. If the drawn card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two (+2)** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk a challenge.) | | **Wild Draw Four Challenge** | If a player believes the previous player illegally used a Wild Draw Four, they can challenge.
• If the challenged player *does* have a playable card of the current color, the challenger must draw six cards (instead of four).
• If the challenged player *does not* have a playable card, the challenger draws four cards. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have only one card left, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn.
• If you forget and another player calls it out before the next turn starts, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The first player to discard all their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of the cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip, Reverse, Draw Two = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each.
Winner’s score = sum of opponents’ points. | | **Game End** | Play continues until a player reaches the agreed‑upon total (e.g., 500 points). | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of the current color** – even after a Wild, the chosen color stays active until changed again. 2. **Use Draw Two/Draw Four strategically** – stack them if you’re allowed (some house rules let players stack +2 or +4). 3. **Watch for “UNO”** – it’s a simple but powerful penalty. 4. **Plan your hand** – try to keep a mix of colors and numbers so you’re never stuck. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
